questions.q: If 31 January 2009 was a Saturday, then what was the day of the week on 30 January 2013?
questions.solution:
Given : 31 January 2009 was a Saturday

Now, 31 January 2009 to 31 January 2013 = 4 Years.

And, 4 years has 1 leap and 3 ordinary year

So total odd days = (1 × 2) + (3 × 1) = 2 + 3 = 5 odd days.

So, 31 January 2013 = Saturday + 5 = Thursday.

But, we need to find the day on 30 January 2013, so subtract 1 day from 31 January 2013.

Therefore, 30 January 2013 will be Thursday - 1 = Wednesday.

Hence, "Wednesday" is the correct answer.

questions.q: Non-Tax revenue is part of _.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Revenue Receipts. Key Points

• Non-tax revenue refers to the income generated by the government from sources other than taxes, such as fees, fines, and grants.

• It is a part of revenue receipts, which are the inflows of funds to the government from all sources.

• The approximations of non-tax revenue receipts from a range of sources, including interest, fees, fines, and other miscellaneous receipts collected during the exercise of sovereign functions, regulatory and license fees, and user fees for goods and services made available to the public.

Additional Information

• Revenue expenditure refers to the expenses incurred by the government on day-to-day activities and welfare programs.

• Revenue expenditures are basically the same as operating expenses because they comprise the costs necessary to cover a business's continuous operating costs.

• Capital expenditure is the spending on long-term investments such as infrastructure and equipment.

• A company uses capital expenditures to pay for the purchase, upkeep, and improvement of tangible assets like real estate, machinery, buildings, plants, and technology.

• Capital receipts are the funds raised by the government through borrowings and disinvestment of assets.

• Income that increases liabilities or decreases financial assets is referred to as a capital receipt.

• They also make mention of cash inflows.

• Both debt and non-debt receipts are considered capital receipts.

questions.q: In which Biosphere Reserve is the largest endangered marine mammal Dugong i.e., Dugong dugon and sea turtles also found?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve. Key Points

• The Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve is home to the largest population of endangered marine mammal Dugong dugon and various species of sea turtles.

• The reserve is located in the Indian state of Tamil Nadu and covers an area of 10,500 square kilometers.

• The Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve is also known for its rich biodiversity and coral reefs.

• The reserve is a popular tourist destination and offers various activities such as snorkeling, diving, and island hopping.

Additional Information

• Khangchendzonga Biosphere Reserve is located in the Indian state of Sikkim and is home to various species of flora and fauna, including the endangered snow leopard.

• ​It became the first "Mixed Heritage" site in India when it was added to the UNESCO World Heritage Sites list in July 2016.

• Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve is located in the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh and is known for its rich biodiversity and various species of flora and fauna.

• In the Rayalaseema region of Andhra Pradesh, India, the Annamayya and Tirupati Districts are home to the majority of the Seshachalam hill ranges.

• Pachmarhi Biosphere Reserve is located in the Indian state of Madhya Pradesh and is known for its unique geological and ecological features.

• The Indian government set up the conservation area in 1999.

• Animals from the lower Western Ghats and the Himalayan Mountains are also included.

questions.q: Which year census is the 15th National census survey conducted by the Census Organisation of India?

• The main aim of the census survey is to collect demographic and socio-economic data of the population of India.

• The census helps in the allocation of resources and planning of government policies.

• The 2011 census was the largest census survey ever conducted in the history of India, covering a population of over 1.2 billion people.

Additional Information

• 1991 was the 13th National census survey.

• 2001 was the 14th National census survey

• The process of methodically gathering, documenting, and computing population data about the individuals within a specific population is known as a census.

• Henry Walter conducted the first known citizen census in Daac (Dhaka) in 1830.

• Henry Walter is regarded as the father of the Indian Census as a result.

• The railway covers a distance of 46 km and passes through 208 curves, 16 tunnels, and over 250 bridges.

• ​It is 164 km long and passes through the Kangra Valley's sub-Himalayan region.

• It is tentatively listed as one of the UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

• The Matheran Hill Railway is a narrow-gauge heritage railway in Maharashtra that connects Neral to Matheran.

• ​It connects Neral to Matheran in the Western Ghats and spans a distance of 21 km, slicing through a forest.

• The Kalka-Shimla Railway is a narrow-gauge railway in Himachal Pradesh that connects Kalka to Shimla.

• It is 2 ft 6 and narrow-gauge.

questions.q: In how many agro-climatic zones has Tamil Nadu been classified?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 7. Key Points

• Tamil Nadu has been classified into 7 agro-climatic zones based on factors such as rainfall, temperature, and soil type.

• These zones are important for agricultural planning and management, as different crops and practices may be more suitable in different zones.

• It is worth noting that the classification of agro-climatic zones may change over time as the climate and other factors evolve.

Additional Information

• The Cauvery Delta, North Eastern, Western, North Western, High Altitude, Southern, and High Rainfall are the seven sub-agroclimatic zones.

• The majority of the state of Tamil Nadu is classified as having either black, red, laterite, or alluvial soil.

• Cyclonic damage is prone to occur frequently in the Northeast region.

• During the southwest monsoon, 400 mm of rain fall on the North Western zone.

• The Western zone experiences 45 rainy days with an average annual rainfall of 715 mm, of which 49% falls during the northeast monsoon season. ​

• In the Cauvery delta region, 984 mm of rain falls on average each year, with over half of that amount coming from northeast monsoon rains.

• A total of 43 rainy days yield an annual mean rainfall of 857 mm in the Southern zone, of which 400 mm come from Northeast monsoon rains.

• The High Rainfall Zone experiences 64 rainy days with an average annual rainfall of 1420 mm.

• The Nilgiris, Kodaikanal, Shevroy, Elagir Javadhi, Kollimalai, Pachamalai, Yercaud, Anamalais, Palani, and Podhigaimalai are all included in the hill and high altitude zone. ​

The correct answer is Wheat, rice. Key Points

• The first phase of the Green Revolution was focused on increasing the yield of wheat and rice crops.

• Wheat and rice were chosen because they are staple food crops in many parts of the world.

• The regions where the Green Revolution was implemented include South Asia, Mexico, and parts of South America.

• The Green Revolution aimed to increase food production and reduce poverty by introducing high-yielding crop varieties, modern farming techniques, and irrigation systems.

Additional Information

• The Green Revolution was a period of agricultural innovation that began in the 1940s and continued through the 1960s and 1970s.

• The term "Green Revolution" was coined by William Gaud, a director at the United States Agency for International Development (USAID), in 1968.

• The Green Revolution had a significant impact on global food production and helped to alleviate hunger and poverty in many developing countries.

• In addition to wheat and rice, the Green Revolution also led to the development of high-yielding varieties of other crops, including maize, sorghum, and soybeans.

questions.q: What was the period of Harshavardhana's reign?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 606 CE to 647 CE. Key Points

• Harshavardhana was a ruler of the Indian subcontinent who ruled from 606 CE to 647 CE.

• The period of Harshavardhana's reign is considered to be the golden age of ancient India, as it was marked by significant cultural and intellectual achievements.​

Additional Information

• An emperor of Pushyabhuti was Harshavardhana.

• He was the younger brother of Rajyavardhana, the king of Thanesar, modern-day Haryana, and the son of Prabhakaravardhana, who had driven out the Alchon Hun invaders.

• He ultimately chose Kannauj as his capital, and he ruled there until 647 CE.

• When Harsha attempted to extend his empire into the southern peninsula of India, he was routed by Emperor Pulakeshin II of the Chalukya dynasty in the Battle of Narmada.

questions.q: While historians use the term Vijayanagara Empire and contemporaries of this empire described it as the _.

questions.q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution empowers the Supreme Court to review its own judgements or orders?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Article 137. Key Points

• Article 137 of the Indian Constitution empowers the Supreme Court to review its own judgements or orders.

• This power is known as the power of 'judicial review'.

• The Supreme Court can exercise this power in cases where there has been an error apparent on the face of the record or where there has been a miscarriage of justice.

• This power is an important aspect of the separation of powers in the Indian Constitution, as it allows the judiciary to check and balance the actions of the executive and legislative branches of government.

Additional Information

• Article 138 of the Indian Constitution deals with the Enlargement of the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court.

• Article 135 of the Indian Constitution deals with the Jurisdiction and powers of the Federal Court under existing law to be exercisable by the Supreme Court.

• Article 136 of the Indian Constitution deals with the Special leave to appeal by the Supreme Court.

questions.q: For the political education of the people at the local level, who brought the resolution on local self-government?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Lord Ripon. Key Points

• Lord Ripon brought the resolution on local self-government in India in 1882.

• This resolution is also known as the Ripon Resolution or the Resolution on Local Self-Government.

• This resolution aimed to transfer some powers and responsibilities from the British government to the local bodies or municipalities.

• This resolution was a significant step towards decentralization and democratization of the Indian political system.

Additional Information

• Lord Mayo was the Viceroy of India from 1869 to 1872, before Lord Ripon.

• Lord Mayo established the Land-improvement Act and the Departments of Revenue, Agriculture, and Commerce on June 9, 1871.

• He made a strong case for Indians' need for a basic education.

• Lord Canning was the Governor-General of India during the Indian Rebellion of 1857.

• ​After the Indian government was transferred from the British East India Company to the crown, Canning oversaw its reorganization.

• In 1859, he was granted an earldom.

• He reorganized his executive council by instituting departmental distribution of responsibilities through the Indian Councils Act of 1861.

• Lord Lytton was the Viceroy of India from 1876 to 1880, after Lord Northbrook.

• Because of the way he handled the Second Anglo-Afghan War and the Great Indian Famine of 1876–1878, he is widely considered as a merciless viceroy.

questions.q: Which of the following elements has variable valency?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Iron. Key Points

• Iron is the only element among the options that has variable valency, meaning it can have different valence states or oxidation numbers depending on the chemical compound it forms.

• The valency of iron can range from +2 to +6, with the most common ones being +2 and +3.

• Sodium, on the other hand, has a fixed valency of +1 in most of its compounds.

• Sulphur usually has a valency of -2 in its compounds, but it can also have valencies of +4, +6, and even +2 in some cases.

• Magnesium has a fixed valency of +2 in its compounds, and it is not known to exhibit variable valency.

Additional Information

• Iron is a transition metal that is widely used in industry and technology due to its magnetic, electrical, and catalytic properties.

• Sodium is a highly reactive alkali metal that is essential for many biological processes and is commonly used in chemical synthesis and metallurgy.

• Sulphur is a non-metallic element that is abundant in nature and has diverse applications in agriculture, medicine, and industry.

• Magnesium is an alkaline earth metal that is important for human health and is used in various applications such as alloys, pyrotechnics, and construction materials.

questions.q:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. And also, they contribute to the development of social and environmental solutions for the planet's future.

B. Companies do play an important role in modern society.

C. Because of their systematic relevance and their impact on policy-making, companies must use their influence in ways that benefit the public good.

D. Some corporations have become so large that their activities and strategic decisions have a direct impact on government policy and citizens' lives.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: BDCA.

Key Points

• Sentence B ("Companies do play an important role in modern society.") – This is the introductory sentence. It sets the context by stating the significance of companies in society, creating a general idea about their importance before moving into specific details.

• Sentence D ("Some corporations have become so large that their activities and strategic decisions have a direct impact on government policy and citizens' lives.") – This sentence logically follows the introduction in Sentence B. It elaborates on the role of companies mentioned in B by explaining how some corporations influence government policies and citizens' lives due to their size and strategic decisions.

• Sentence C ("Because of their systematic relevance and their impact on policy-making, companies must use their influence in ways that benefit the public good.") – This sentence builds on the idea presented in D. It emphasizes the responsibility of companies to use their influence for the public good, given their substantial impact on policy-making and society.

• Sentence A ("And also, they contribute to the development of social and environmental solutions for the planet's future.") – This serves as a concluding thought, highlighting another positive aspect of companies. It reinforces the idea that companies not only influence policies but also contribute to social and environmental solutions.

Hence, option 4 (BDCA) is correct because it presents the ideas in a coherent manner: starting with the role of companies, moving into their influence, addressing their responsibilities, and finally concluding with their contributions.

questions.q:
Select the grammatically correct sentence.

A. As a nation, India is a united country and shall always remain so.

B. As nation, India is a united country and shall always remain so.

C. As the nation, India is a united country and shall always remain so.

D. As a nation, India is an united country and shall always remain so.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: "As a nation, India is a united country and shall always remain so."

Key Points

• The sentence is grammatically correct because it uses the indefinite article "a" before "nation" to show that India is one of many nations, and not the only one.

• It also uses the correct verb tense, "shall always remain," to indicate a future certainty.

• The sentence is structured properly with a subject ("India"), verb ("is"), and predicate ("a united country").

• The phrase "as a nation" is used correctly to introduce the subject of the sentence.

• The sentence is well-structured, with a clear subject-verb agreement and coherence in expressing the idea that India is currently a united country and will continue to be so in the future.

Therefore, the correct answer is option 1

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

The magazine house was expecting unpublished authors for their forthcoming exclusive issue on new trends.
options: Unpublished authors will be expected by the magazine house for their forthcoming exclusive issue on new trends.
Unpublished authors were being expected by the magazine house for their forthcoming exclusive issue on new trends.
Unpublished authors was expected by the magazine house for their forthcoming exclusive issue on new trends.
Unpublished authors were expected by the magazine house for their forthcoming exclusive issue on new trends.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Unpublished authors were being expected by the magazine house for their forthcoming exclusive issue on new trends.

Key Points

• The sentence is in the active voice with the subject "the magazine house" performing the action of "expecting" on the object "unpublished authors".

• To convert it into passive voice, we need to make the object the subject and add a form of the verb "to be" before the past participle of the main verb.

• In this case, "unpublished authors" becomes the subject and "were being expected" is the passive form of "was expecting".

• The preposition "by" is added to show who is performing the action (the magazine house).

Therefore, the correct answer is option 2.
